items.title: Flow requires challenge matching skill
items.claim: Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi's flow research (1975 onwards) identified conditions for the optimal experience. What characterises flow?

options.text: Challenge matched to skill (slightly stretching), clear goals, immediate feedback, deep concentration, sense of control, loss of self-consciousness, time distortion

items.reveal:
Csikszentmihalyi's Experience Sampling Method (ESM, 1975) gave participants pagers; when paged at random they noted what they were doing and how they felt. The pattern: deep enjoyment occurred when skill and challenge were both high.

Too little challenge → boredom; too much → anxiety. Sports psychology uses flow frameworks for performance preparation. Critics (Engeser 2012) note flow may be more available in certain activity types and that measurement post-hoc is suspect.
items.why: Flow describes a measurable state but doesn't make it easy to engineer. The conditions can be designed for; the experience can't be commanded.

items.title: Type A personality's link to heart disease has weakened
items.claim: Friedman and Rosenman's 1959 'Type A' personality (competitive, impatient, hostile) was linked to coronary heart disease. What does the more recent evidence show?

options.text: Type A is the strongest predictor of heart disease
The composite Type A construct has weak predictive value in modern studies; hostility specifically (Williams 1989 onwards) retains some predictive power, while time-urgency and competitiveness do not
Type A reduces heart disease risk

items.reveal_title: Hostility, not the full Type A
items.reveal:
Friedman and Rosenman's 1976 follow-up of the Western Collaborative Group Study showed Type A nearly doubled CHD risk. Meta-analyses since the 1990s (Myrtek 2001) found weak overall effects for Type A; hostility/anger components retained predictive power.

The broader pattern: complex personality categories often decompose under empirical scrutiny into more specific traits with different effects.
items.why: Popular psychology preserves the original construct long after research has narrowed it. Specific hostility, not generic 'Type A', is what carries the cardiovascular signal.
